topics: Inference runtime upgrade and canary plan
transcript:
Header: 2027-08-19 10:00 PDT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Alex Kim, Priya Desai (Redwood) - Jason Miller, Rita Gomez, Tom Wu (Aurora)

Summary: quick sync on pilot status, network blockers, perf deviations after runtime upgrade, agreed test plan and documentation updates.

00:00:05 - Alex Kim: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh good to see you all. quick agenda: networking, routing, perf from last upgrade, and next steps.
00:00:22 - Jason Miller: yeah thanks, Alex. we had the infra team on because we hit that TLS handshakes spike after you pushed the runtime 1.3.2 build last week.
00:00:35 - Priya Desai: right, and we saw higher tail latency on a subset of requests that require KV cache warming. looked like about 120 to 150 ms extra p95 on cold-shots, not all calls.
00:00:50 - Tom Wu: and to add, on our side some requests route through a different AZ because of the k8s node autoscaler. that might explain some variance.
00:01:05 - Rita Gomez: quick security note, we're still waiting for final inbound NSG rules for the pilot. we've got the outbound rules locked but need the explicit allow list for the Redwood control plane IPs.
00:01:18 - Alex Kim: got it. Jason, can you confirm who's owner for firewall changes?
00:01:24 - Jason Miller: yeah that's on Rita and network team, but I can help accelerate. we can probably push it this week if we get the exact IP list.
00:01:35 - Priya Desai: Alex, we shared a short runbook and network diagram draft last week - I can update with the control-plane / data-plane split and mark which CIDR needs peering.
00:01:49 - Alex Kim: perfect. please call out the peering route table entries and the NAT behavior.
00:01:56 - Rita Gomez: question on peering: are we doing VPC peering or using Transit Gateway? there was a mention of TGW in the doc but our security prefers peering for isolation.
00:02:10 - Priya Desai: for the pilot we recommended VPC peering to keep things simpler; TGW is an option for scale later. we'll annotate pros/cons in the runbook.
00:02:23 - Tom Wu: from perf tests, we did a couple of replay runs yesterday and saw the NVidia driver upgrade changed GPU scheduling slightly - some pods got preempted when node CPU hit the burst threshold. not a Redwood issue per se but it affects tail latency.
00:02:40 - Alex Kim: ok noted. that ties to the canary plan for runtime upgrades - we should ensure node autoscaler thresholds don't kick in during bench runs.
00:02:52 - Jason Miller: we'll pin min nodes for the next bench.
00:02:56 - Priya Desai: anything on the routing layer? the ingress NGINX version: we suggested moving to 1.25 to fix a connection reuse bug. that change should reduce TLS handshake overhead.
00:03:10 - Rita Gomez: is 1.25 compatible with our AppGateway? our infra has some managed LB quirks.
00:03:18 - Priya Desai: yes, we've tested 1.25 in a mirror cluster; we'll share the config diff. small note: change the keepalive settings and enable TLS session resumption.
00:03:31 - Tom Wu: how about cert rotation - we run cert-manager; will session resumption survive cert changes?
00:03:39 - Alex Kim: session resumption will break during rotation briefly; we recommend a staged rollout and test under low traffic. that's in the runbook.
00:03:48 - Jason Miller: can we get a one-page checklist for the NGINX upgrade? that'll help us coordinate with infra.
00:03:54 - Priya Desai: yes, I'll prepare a checklist and share in the runbook doc.
00:04:05 - Alex Kim: on KV cache cold-start: Priya, you mentioned a mitigation for warming the KV on deploy?
00:04:12 - Priya Desai: right, we have a background warmup step that streams top-k prefixes; for now it's experimental. we saw it reduce cold p95 by about 80 ms in our lab. we'll run in staging and capture traces.
00:04:27 - Tom Wu: can that warmup be parallelized across shards? our embedding traffic patterns are bursty and a single-thread warmup is too slow.
00:04:36 - Priya Desai: yes, it supports parallel warmup; we just need to tune batch sizes to match your shard count. I'll include recommended parameters.
00:04:45 - Rita Gomez: security-wise, will warmup touch any PII? we need to ensure data residency - only synthetic tokens.
00:04:53 - Priya Desai: yes, warmup uses synthetic prefixes only. no customer data. we'll add that note to the runbook.
00:05:02 - Jason Miller: earlier you mentioned control plane IPs - can you paste that list in the doc?
00:05:08 - Alex Kim: yes, I'll paste the current shortlist; final list may expand during GA.
00:05:14 - Tom Wu: about telemetry, our APM is showing correlation between failed TLS handshakes and a small fraction of clients using older cipher suites. is Redwood requiring TLS1.3?
00:05:25 - Priya Desai: we default to TLS1.3 on the control plane for security, but dataplane to customer can negotiate 1.2 if needed. we'll provide recommended ciphers.
00:05:36 - Rita Gomez: ok please add the cipher list; we have a compliance scanner that will validate it.
00:05:44 - Alex Kim: switching gears - testing plan for next week: Priya will run routing + handshake perf tests, Tom will run model warmup validation on staging, Rita will finalize firewall rules.
00:05:58 - Jason Miller: timeline good, can we reconvene same time next week?
00:06:03 - Alex Kim: yes, same slot next Friday. any blockers?
00:06:07 - Tom Wu: one minor blocker: the staging cluster still has the older kernel on two nodes; that changes NIC offload behavior. we're patching this afternoon.
00:06:18 - Priya Desai: if you can patch, please notify us; the perf runs should be after the patch.
00:06:23 - Jason Miller: noted. we'll coordinate.
00:06:28 - Priya Desai: also, on the canary rollback policy - we suggested automatic rollback if p99 increases > 10% over baseline for 15 minutes. any thoughts?
00:06:38 - Rita Gomez: sounds reasonable but we need alerting to the on-call pager.
00:06:42 - Alex Kim: we can wire alerts to your pager via SNS; I'll coordinate with your on-call.
00:06:49 - Tom Wu: and for metrics, please include GPU utilization and kernel queue depth as part of the canary dashboard.
00:06:57 - Priya Desai: will do.
00:07:00 - Alex Kim: quick note on cost: Aurora asked about Dedicated vs Private economics; we gave a rough estimate last call - if you want I can share a more detailed comparison.
00:07:10 - Jason Miller: yes please, that'll help leadership decide for Q4 budgeting.
00:07:15 - Alex Kim: will send a short cost worksheet.
00:07:20 - Jason Miller: ok thanks.
00:07:24 - Priya Desai: any questions on the runtime build? we tracked a small mem increase in 1.3.2 due to a new prefetching heuristic. we can toggle the flag off for the pilot if you'd prefer.
00:07:36 - Tom Wu: toggle it off for now, let's keep mem stable.
00:07:40 - Priya Desai: noted, we'll push a config flip in staging.
00:07:44 - Rita Gomez: last compliance question - will logs include plaintext request tokens? our policy forbids that.
00:07:52 - Alex Kim: Redwood's Private option masks request tokens in logs by default and supports customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest. we'll add the logging configuration section to the runbook draft.
00:08:03 - Jason Miller: great.
00:08:08 - Alex Kim: recap and owners: Alex to send IP list and updated diagram; Priya will produce NGINX checklist and run perf tests; Rita to share firewall rules; Tom to validate warmup. agree?
00:08:20 - All: yes/affirmative.
00:08:24 - Alex Kim: ok i'll follow up with links: runbook (link), perf spreadsheet (link), and the one-pager for NGINX upgrade.
00:08:33 - Priya Desai: i'll also attach the config diff and recommended keepalives.
00:08:38 - Jason Miller: thanks, see you next week.
00:08:41 - Alex Kim: thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.

Notes: Shared artifacts referenced during call: runbook (https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/aurora-pilot), perf spreadsheet (https://drive.example.com/aurora-pilot-perf), nginx-checklist draft (attached in runbook).

End of transcript.
